description: Implement pearl-guard crate: the pre/post guard engine that enforces Article 7 (fail-closed). Guards are evaluated before and after task execution. Each guard is a registered capability of type Guard that gets invoked via the script runtime. The engine evaluates guards in order, and if any guard denies, the operation is blocked. Fail-closed: if a guard cannot be reached or crashes, the operation is denied. Reference: small_daily_tasks hooks/pre_bash_guard.py pattern and daily_rust/agentflow-harness-rust src/policy.rs PolicyGuard pattern.
steps: Create crates/pearl-guard/Cargo.toml depending on pearl-core, pearl-governance (CapabilityManifest, OnError), pearl-runtime (RuntimeAdapter, ScriptSpec, RuntimeResult), serde, serde_json, thiserror, chrono. Use workspace.dependencies.
Add pearl-guard to workspace members in /projects/sandbox/pearl/Cargo.toml and add pearl-guard = { path = 'crates/pearl-guard' } to [workspace.dependencies].
Create crates/pearl-guard/src/lib.rs with module doc explaining Article 7 enforcement: guards fail-closed, hooks fail-open, and this crate makes that distinction structural.
Define GuardVerdict enum: Allow { reason: Option<String> }, Deny { reason: String, guard_id: String }.
Define GuardContext struct: the input to a guard evaluation - task_id, capability_id, command (the shell command or script being guarded), environment (BTreeMap), execution_phase (Pre or Post).
Define ExecutionPhase enum: Pre (before execution), Post (after execution, before verification).
Implement GuardRule struct representing one guard rule (inline, not requiring a subprocess): id, patterns (Vec<regex::Regex> or Vec<String>), reason, tag, phase.

Implement InlineGuardEngine for fast regex-based guards (like pre_bash_guard.py rules) that operate without spawning a subprocess. Rules are loaded from a GuardRuleSet (Vec<GuardRule>). Method: evaluate(context: &GuardContext) -> GuardVerdict.

Implement ScriptGuardEngine for guards that are external scripts (capabilities of type Guard). Method: evaluate(context: &GuardContext, manifest: &CapabilityManifest) -> GuardVerdict. This invokes the guard script with context as JSON input, reads the verdict from stdout JSON, and enforces fail-closed (crash/timeout/no-output => Deny).
Implement GuardChain that holds multiple guards (inline + script) and evaluates them in order. First Deny wins. All Allow => Allow. Any error => Deny (fail-closed).

Implement default_rules() that returns the standard set of inline guard rules matching the reference patterns: cloud-api-guard (6 LLM API hosts), destructive-rm, force-push-main, no-verify-smuggle, sensitive-env-read, sensitive-exfil.

Write comprehensive tests: inline guard blocks destructive rm, inline guard allows safe commands, fail-closed on error, GuardChain short-circuits on first Deny, default rules match reference patterns from small_daily_tasks.
Ensure cargo test --workspace passes, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.
acceptance_criteria: InlineGuardEngine correctly blocks commands matching destructive patterns
Default rules block cloud LLM API calls
findings: All 344 workspace tests pass (41 new in pearl-guard, 303 existing unchanged). Clippy clean. Fmt clean. The regex crate was added directly to pearl-guard's Cargo.toml as instructed (not as a workspace dependency). InlineGuardEngine provides fast regex evaluation matching all 6 reference patterns from pre_bash_guard.py. ScriptGuardEngine delegates to RuntimeAdapter with fail-closed semantics. GuardChain composes both strategies with first-deny-wins ordering.
